summary: Feed s132_double is degraded: 100% of packets are untagged (VLANs 10,20 missing) and IDS 1 Gbps port is overloaded by 1.68 Gbps microbursts (168% capacity).

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP/SPAN aggregation is stripping 802.1Q tags or delivering via access/untagged port instead of trunk passthrough. All packets arrive untagged so required VLANs 10 and 20 are never seen.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS loses tenant/segment context for VLANs 10 and 20, cannot apply VLAN-aware policies or detect lateral movement/cross-VLAN violations, creating blind spots for detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Preserve and forward 802.1Q tags end-to-end from TAP through packet broker to IDS so VLANs 10 and 20 are visible for IDS classification and correlation.

findings.root_cause: Traffic microbursts peak at 1.68 Gbps in 1ms intervals, exceeding the IDS 1 Gbps port capacity by 68%. Packet broker is forwarding line-rate bursts without shaping or distribution, causing 4 overloaded intervals.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS with 1 Gbps port and needs_full_payload=true will drop packets during bursts, causing missed signatures, broken flow reassembly, and incomplete detection. IDS cannot keep up with burst rate.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute flows across 2x1G IDS ports or a higher-speed port via load balancing to absorb 1.68 Gbps bursts without drops; slicing/filtering not suitable because IDS needs full payload and both directions.
